key_insight: PMTM retains and updates tumor evidence across imaging scales to segment brain tumors when one or more MRI sequences are unavailable.
clinical_relevance: This imaging study—not a drug discovery study—could support tumor delineation with incomplete MRI inputs, but clinical utility remains unestablished.
method: Accepts any non-empty subset of T1ce, T1, FLAIR, and T2 MRI.
Pools modality evidence into a compact subject-specific memory, updated through a learned gate across encoder stages.
Uses memory-guided residual fusion, modality-token mixing, and semantic supervision at four stages.
evidence_signal: Across all 15 non-empty modality subsets and three tumor regions, mean Dice scores were 75.31%, 77.54%, and 80.47% on BraTS2018, BraTS2020, and BraTS2023 GLI, respectively, exceeding RobustSeg, RFNet, and mmFormer in the reported experiments.
watch_item: Benchmark results do not establish prospective clinical performance or robustness to real-world MRI acquisition differences.
paper_title: Progressive multi-scale tumor-state memory for incomplete multimodal brain tumor segmentation
